## Implementation Report — round 1

**Status:** READY-FOR-REVIEW

### (a) what files changed

- `scripts/issue494_predictor_192.py` (new, ~390 LOC): Phase 2 driver. Imports + reuses every predictor helper from the Phase 1 driver (cosine a/b, JS RB, fact-slice JS, vLLM bystander prior). Per-stratum + pooled Spearman with seed-stratified cluster-aware bootstrap CI (5000 reps, within-substrate resampling per Davison & Hinkley 1997 Ch. 3). ### (b) why these changes
The plan's §4 design splits #494 into three phases with one driver each:

- **Phase 1 re-runs the inline-444 predictors under canonical recipe** because the inline analysis (`eval_results/issue_444/persona_distance_topic/results.json` `config`) ran at `js_r=6, js_max_tok=48`, NOT the canonical `R=8 / max_tokens=256` defined in `.claude/rules/persona-distance-metrics.md` L18-L34. Pooling #494's #192 numbers (which WILL be at canonical) against the inline-444 numbers at a different recipe would conflate recipe drift with substrate effect. The fix is to recompute #444 at canonical alongside #192. cosine_a / bystander_logprob / fact_slice_js are recipe-independent by construction (no sampling), so the consistency gate at the end of Phase 1 doubles as a regression check — if those three quantities diverge from inline by >1e-4 there's a code-path bug in the recompute, not a recipe effect.
- **Phase 2 is the substantive value-add** the inline-444 analysis did not do: extend the same predictor recipe to a second substrate (#192's positive-only Lin/Pavlek rig) with a different fact, different teacher, different bystander panel, different training regime. The 4 predictors per cell test the open-questions trailer's reference-frame hypothesis on a within-rig + across-rig basis the single-substrate inline analysis cannot. Probe subset n=30 (vs full 150) is justified in plan §4.2: DV resolution is 8 cells not 150, so larger probe counts only tighten the per-cell predictor mean for diminishing returns at the re-analysis budget (per-cell SE 30^-1/2 ≈ 0.18 vs 150^-1/2 ≈ 0.08 for 5× compute; #444 ran at n=60 so #192 at n=30 is only 1.4× noisier per cell).
- **Phase 3 is pooled + per-stratum** because substrates are heterogeneous (#192 is positive-only with leakage clustered tightly ~58-65%; #444's three contrastive recipes have leakage spread 0.02-0.99) and pooling them blindly conflates two leakage regimes. The plan pre-registered per-stratum Spearman + pooled Spearman with substrate as a fixed factor; the cluster-aware bootstrap (sample-with-replacement within each substrate) preserves stratification, avoiding the unstratified bootstrap's bias toward whichever stratum has the wider spread. Partial Spearman tests the trailer's claim that the prior survives controlling for distance and distance does not survive controlling for prior.

The single-script-per-phase architecture matches the plan §4.8 smoke/sweep parity statement — no multi-cell launcher, no subprocess dispatch, smoke IS production with `--smoke` flags that reduce to 1 cell.

## (b) Considered but not done
- **Off-topic null reference (Betley probe set across both substrates).** Plan §5 lists this as a separate condition; §9 auto-descope order has it as priority-1 drop. I did NOT wire it in this round — the headline path is the on-topic predictors, and the auto-descope says drop off-topic first if compute runs over. If the headline pass shows the on-topic story is interesting, the off-topic null is a 1h GPU-h follow-up on the same scripts (add `--off-topic-probes` flag, fetch from `issue404_common.fetch_preregistered_probes`). Defer.
- **Per-probe-family JS slice for #444 A-family.** The plan calls out `js_sliced_by_probe_type.png` as part of the exploratory dump; the current Phase 1 driver aggregates JS to a single per-(persona, recipe) value, not per-family. The Phase 3 figure for this is a stub (a labeled placeholder). A per-family slice is a Phase-1 driver code-path: change `js_vs_reference_canonical` to return per-probe JS, group by `build_reformulation_probes` keys. I left it out because (a) the plan's headline tests don't require it and (b) the inline-444 analysis didn't slice it either, so cross-comparison stays cleanest at the aggregate level.
- **Off-loading the HF model BEFORE vLLM via process fork.** The current pattern is `del model; gc.collect(); torch.cuda.empty_cache(); torch.cuda.synchronize()`. Per CLAUDE.md gotchas, vLLM worker subprocesses can survive a `del` and re-allocate freed GPU memory. I followed the inline-444 pattern (single Python process, sequential HF → vLLM phases within one script) because the inline-444 scripts run cleanly that way. If the production launch hits an OOM at the vLLM phase, fall back to splitting Phase 1 into two SSH-invoked subprocesses (one for HF predictors, one for the vLLM prior). Flagged in (d) needs-human-eyeball.
- **Pre-computed bystander_logprob reuse from inline-444.** The inline-444 `eval_results/issue_444/bystander_logprob/logprob_results.json` is recipe-independent and could be read out instead of re-computed. I chose to re-compute because (a) the plan §4.1 explicitly calls for the recompute as a consistency check, (b) re-running the vLLM teacher-force on 6 personas × 239 teach rows is ~5 min (a tiny fraction of the budget), and (c) the consistency-check block then doubles as a code-path validation.
- **Storing the per-probe JS values + per-response sampled tokens.** I store the per-cell aggregate but not the per-probe / per-response trajectories. Per-probe JS would enable a probe-family slice (see above); per-response samples would enable a downstream analyzer to spot-check the on-policy distribution. Skipped for budget; if the analyzer needs per-probe JS, re-run with a `--keep-per-probe` flag.

## (d) Needs human eyeball
- **The vLLM-after-HF GPU-handoff pattern.** Phase 1 + Phase 2 each load the HF model first (cosine a/b + JS + fact-slice), then `_drop_model(model)` and load vLLM for the bystander prior. The `_drop_model` helper does `del model; gc.collect(); torch.cuda.empty_cache(); torch.cuda.synchronize()` — the inline-444 pattern. Per CLAUDE.md "vLLM worker-subprocess teardown" gotcha, this can fail if vLLM worker subprocesses survive across phases; the inline-444 scripts didn't hit this because they ran ONE phase per script invocation. If the production smoke shows the vLLM phase OOMs after the HF phase, the fix is to split each Phase into two `nohup`-chained scripts.
- **The Phase 1 consistency-gate tolerance (1e-4).** The inline-444 numbers come from a different HF Transformers + vLLM version snapshot; deterministic forward passes with bfloat16 weights can drift by ~1e-5 across HF version bumps. 1e-4 is the plan-specified tolerance. If the gate FAILs by a hair (say 1e-4 < diff < 1e-3), that's a version drift not a code bug; the appropriate response is to widen the tolerance + flag the inline-444 numbers as "from an older snapshot" in the clean-result rather than block Phase 2.
- **#192 Arm B teach prompt overlap.** The Qwen-default teach prompt (`"You are Qwen, created by Alibaba Cloud. You are a helpful assistant."`) overlaps lexically with the `assistant` bystander (`"You are a helpful assistant."`) and is similar to `no_system`. The plan §4.2 + §5 + §8 (Risks row) flag this; the analyzer should report Arm B with-and-without the `assistant` bystander as a sensitivity check. The driver doesn't apply this filter — it reports all 4 bystanders per arm.
- **The `js_sliced_by_probe_type` placeholder figure.** Currently emits a text-stub PNG; the analyzer should either populate from a per-family JS rerun (~30 min on the same driver with a `--per-family` flag) or remove from the clean-result figure list.

## Issues Found

### Critical (block merge)

#### 1. `scripts/issue494_regress.py:50` — JS sign-convention inversion vs inline-444 (the single most consequential bug)

**Evidence:** `PREDICTORS = ["cosine_a_L21", "cosine_b_L21", "js_on_topic", "bystander_logprob", "fact_slice_js"]`

The new code stores `js_on_topic` as **raw JS distance** (`_js_from_logprobs` returns the base-2 JS in `[0,1]`, distance not similarity — `scripts/issue494_predictor_444.py:318` `return float(js.clamp(0, 1).mean())`). But the inline-444 published headline `correlations.json` reports Spearman ρ values computed against `js_similarity = 1 − JS` (a *similarity*, where higher = closer; `scripts/issue444_persona_distance_topic.py:274` `js_similarity[topic] = {k: (1.0 - v) for k, v in js.items()}`). The same is true for `fact_slice_js` — new code stores raw JS at `scripts/issue494_predictor_444.py:705`, inline-444's `eval_results/issue_444/bystander_logprob/fact_slice_js.json` carries both `js_fact` (raw) and `js_similarity = 1 − js_fact`, and the inline `correlations.json` reports its −0.418 Spearman against `js_similarity`.

The Phase 1 driver DOES already compute `js_similarity_M = 1.0 - js_val` and stores it (line 692-694), but **Phase 3 reads `js_on_topic` (raw JS), not `js_similarity_M`**.

**Confirmed by a smoke run on synthetic stubs:**
```
Pooled Spearman (n=10 synthetic):
  cosine_a_L21              rho=-0.518    (similarity dir, matches inline-444 sign on cosine_on −0.49)
  js_on_topic               rho=+0.570    (distance dir, OPPOSITE sign from inline-444 js_on −0.46)
  fact_slice_js             rho=+0.518    (distance dir, OPPOSITE sign from inline-444 fact_slice_js −0.42)
  bystander_logprob         rho=+0.518    (logprob dir, matches inline-444 +0.27)
Partial Spearman:
  cosine_a_L21_given_prior  rho=-0.245    (similarity dir)
  js_on_topic_given_prior   rho=+0.245    (distance dir — same partial, opposite sign from cosine_a)
```

**Impact (load-bearing):**
- The hero figure title narrates "Hero: pooled n=X; Spearman rho = -0.518" — this is the cosine number, but the regression JSON's `pooled["js_on_topic"]["rho"]` carries the opposite-sign analogue. The analyzer reading both will be sign-confused.
- The `cosine_vs_js_bars` chart puts cosine_a (similarity direction) and `js_on_topic` / `fact_slice_js` (distance direction) on the SAME y-axis. Two bars will visually tell opposite stories about the same H2 hypothesis.
- The `paired_bootstrap_rho_diff` "cosine_a_L21 minus js_on_topic" diff is meaningless — it subtracts a similarity-direction ρ from a distance-direction ρ, conflating sign convention with predictive-power difference.
- The plan's H2 threshold "pooled ρ ≤ −0.30 on the teacher-referenced predictor" is stated for similarity-direction predictors. Against raw JS the same hypothesis maps to `ρ ≥ +0.30`. As written, an H2-supporting JS result will appear to FAIL the H2 threshold.
- The Phase 1 `_consistency_check` already uses the right inversion (line 776 `inline_js_per = {p: 1.0 - INLINE_444_VALUES[p]["js_on_topic_inline_M"] for p in OTHERS}`) — proving the implementer understood the inversion in one place but missed it in Phase 3.

**Fix (one-line):** change `PREDICTORS = [..., "js_on_topic", ...]` to `PREDICTORS = [..., "js_similarity_M", ...]` in `scripts/issue494_regress.py:50` AND store `fact_slice_similarity_M = 1 - fact_slice_js` alongside `fact_slice_js` in `scripts/issue494_predictor_444.py:705` (and the Phase 2 counterpart at `scripts/issue494_predictor_192.py:279`). All downstream figure narration + threshold tests then match the inline-444 sign convention. Alternatively, document explicitly in the regression JSON `_doc` block + every figure caption that JS/fact-slice predictors are stored as DISTANCES with H2-threshold `ρ ≥ +0.30` — but the cleaner fix is to use similarity throughout.

#### 2. `scripts/issue494_predictor_444.py:515` + `:756-768` — Cosine probe-count drift breaks the byte-identity consistency gate

**Evidence:**
- `ap.add_argument("--n-cos-probes", type=int, default=60, ...)` (line 515) — new default = 60 (the full A-family set).
- Inline-444 published cosine values used `n_cos_probes=40` (`eval_results/issue_444/persona_distance_topic/results.json` `config` block: `"n_cos_probes": 40`).
- Consistency gate at lines 759-762: `"cosine_a_L21_diff": abs(results["predictors"][other]["cosine_a_L21"] - inline["cosine_a_L21"])` compared against `tolerance_byte_identical = 1e-4`.

The cosine predictor is averaged across probes (`last_token_acts` returns one residual per probe; `cosine_vs_reference_per_layer` computes per-probe cosine then `float(cos.mean())`). Adding probes 41-60 to the average will not preserve the inline value within 1e-4 unless the additional 20 probes have cosine values within ~5e-4 of the running mean (vanishingly unlikely for different paraphrase families).

`build_reformulation_probes` returns 5 families × 12 paraphrases = exactly 60 probes; first 40 = the inline subset, last 20 = the wikipedia/notable/name_one/fill/trivia tail. The `--n-cos-probes 60` default exercises probes the inline analysis never saw.

**Impact:**
- The Phase 1 consistency gate (`overall_pass`) will return FAIL with `cosine_a_L21_diff > 1e-4`, the script exits with code 2 (line 826), and the chained `&&` halts before Phase 2. The whole pipeline aborts at the Phase 1 gate spuriously — not because of a bug, but because the gate was specified against a probe-count it never matches.

**Fix:** Either
- (a) Set `--n-cos-probes 40` to match inline exactly (production launch + restore that as the default), OR
- (b) Make the consistency check recompute cosine_a on the first 40 probes only (slice `acts_a[other][li][:40]` before the cosine + mean), then compare against inline, OR
- (c) Widen the cosine_a tolerance and document the probe-count change as a deliberate scope difference. (a) is the cleanest. Combined with #1's docs the byte-identity claim becomes defensible.

#### 3. Step 0.6 smoke-run-missing — Phase 1 and Phase 2 have NOT been GPU-smoke-tested

**Evidence:** The implementer's `epm:experiment-implementation v1` `## Smoke run` section:

Phase 1 + Phase 2 sub-sections show only "import + argparse round-trip" — there is no exit code 0, no real artifact digest, and no proof any GPU-dependent code path executed. ### Major

#### 4. `scripts/issue494_predictor_192.py:422-449` — Per-arm vLLM re-load doubles prior compute + risks OOM

**Evidence:** The bystander-prior loop:
```python
for arm_id, _arm in active_arms.items():
    active_for_prior = dict(active_bystanders)
    ...
    prior_results = bystander_logprob_all_personas(args.model, teach_rows, active_for_prior, ...)
```

The comment on lines 424-430 acknowledges: "The bystander prior depends only on the BYSTANDER system prompt, not the teach prompt ... so we could compute it once for all bystanders + cache. We compute it explicitly per arm to keep the output JSON symmetric."

`bystander_logprob_all_personas` at `scripts/issue494_predictor_444.py:388` does a full `LLM(...)` construction on every call. Two arms = TWO sequential vLLM loads, with no explicit teardown of the first.

**Impact:**
- Per CLAUDE.md "vLLM worker-subprocess teardown" gotcha: vLLM worker subprocesses can persist after `del`/`gc.collect()` and re-grab GPU memory. The Phase 2 production run will be the FIRST place this pattern is exercised (Phase 1 only loads vLLM once); a load-twice OOM at the second arm would lose all Phase-2 Arm-B work despite the per-arm JSON checkpoint at line 415-416 (which writes BEFORE the prior).
- Doubles vLLM startup overhead and prior compute (~1-2 min per startup × 2 = ~3-4 min wasted; not catastrophic but unnecessary).

**Fix:** Hoist the prior computation outside the arm loop (it's identical across arms — same bystander system prompts, same teach rows). Compute once, then attach the same per-bystander values to each arm's `results["arms"][arm_id]["bystanders"][byst_id]["bystander_logprob"]`. The "symmetric JSON output" argument the implementer makes is correct as a downstream concern, but the JSON can stay symmetric WITHOUT doing the compute twice — just write the same dict to both arms.

#### 5. Launch command in `(c) how to launch` blocks foreground shell — orchestrator polling will not work

**Evidence:** The implementer's launch:
```bash
nohup uv run python scripts/issue494_predictor_444.py ... \
    > /workspace/logs/issue-494-phase1.log 2>&1 && \
nohup uv run python scripts/issue494_predictor_192.py ... \
    > /workspace/logs/issue-494-phase2.log 2>&1 && \
nohup uv run python scripts/issue494_regress.py ... \
    > /workspace/logs/issue-494-phase3.log 2>&1
```

**Problem:** `nohup` only protects from `SIGHUP`; it does NOT background. Without a trailing `&`, the chained command blocks the shell for the full ~6h wall-clock. The orchestrator's bg-Bash polling loop (which expects launches to return within ~60s) will hang the experimenter agent.

**Fix:** Append `&` to the final command (or pre-pend each `nohup ... &` independently with explicit dependency tracking). Canonical pattern:
```bash
nohup bash -c '<chain>' > /workspace/logs/issue-494-pipeline.log 2>&1 &
disown
```

#### 6. `fact_slice_js` similarity variant not stored

**Evidence:** `scripts/issue494_predictor_444.py:705` stores only raw `fact_slice_js` (distance). The inline-444 `fact_slice_js.json` carries both `js_fact` AND `js_similarity`. Phase 3 reads `fact_slice_js` (distance) into the DataFrame — same sign-flip issue as Critical #1.

**Fix:** Per Critical #1's fix, store a `fact_slice_similarity_M = 1 - fact_slice_js` alongside, OR convert at the regression DataFrame-build step. (Counterpart in Phase 2 at `scripts/issue494_predictor_192.py:279`.)
